duration.cost: Shorter connections finish faster and move less traffic per attempt.

src_bytes.cost: Smaller packets reduce bandwidth footprint but need more connections for the same effect.

dst_bytes.cost: A real SYN flood rarely gets a response anyway; this is already close to zero.

count.cost: Fewer connections per window looks less like a flood, but is a weaker attack.

srv_count.cost: Same tradeoff as connection count, scoped to one service.

serror_rate.reason: Same signature: this rate sitting near 1.0 is what makes it a SYN flood in the first place.

same_srv_rate.cost: Spreading across services looks less targeted, but dilutes the flood.

dst_host_count.cost: Fewer hosts touched per window reduces blast radius and visibility.

dst_host_srv_count.cost: Same tradeoff, scoped to host and service together.

flag_is_error.reason: A SYN flood's whole mechanism is half-open connections; turning this off means it stops being this attack.

logged_in.reason: Faking a successful login means actually compromising valid credentials, a separate problem from anything else in this flow record.

is_priv_port.reason: This identifies which service is being targeted. Changing it means attacking a different service, not evading detection on this one.

duration.cost: Longer pauses between probes look more like normal traffic, but the scan takes longer.

dst_host_count.cost: Fewer hosts probed per window is a slower, quieter sweep.

dst_host_srv_count.cost: Same tradeoff, scoped to host and service together.
